title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 157-159 of the cote; Grothendieck's own numbering 368-370). Grothendieck studies an automorphism u of the profinite outer 'groupe à lacets' π̂_{0,3}, the profinite completion of π_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}) ≅ F̂_2. The automorphism commutes outerly with the S_3 symmetries σ_∞ and ρ, and acts on the loops by a multiplier μ ∈ Ẑ*. In modern terms this is essentially an element (λ = μ, f) of the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT̂, or a slight enlargement of it. He extends u canonically to the profinite completion of the extended group Ŝ^+_{0,3} ≅ SL(2,Z)^∧′, acting trivially on the quotient S_3. He then pushes the action down to the congruence quotient SL(2,Ẑ)′.

Result of the previous page. Theorem (75)-(78): the induced action on SL(2,Ẑ) is conjugation by an explicit matrix u̲ ∈ GL(2,Ẑ), given by
 u̲ = μ(tσ_∞ + u)τ^{α_2} = μ(u, ε_2 t; −t, ε_2 u),
with the following properties:
- det u̲ = μ;
- u̲ normalizes σ_∞ up to the sign ε_2;
- u̲ sends ρ to (ε_2 g)ρ.
Here (−1)^{α_2} = ε_2 is determined by μ mod 4. The matrix commutes with σ_∞ = (0 1; −1 0) up to sign, so it is a Gaussian-type element u + t·i of (Ẑ[i])*, up to the twist τ. The determinant condition amounts to ε_2 μ(t² + u²) = 1, which is used explicitly on the next page.

This page shows the matrix u̲ is canonical modulo sign.
1. The automorphism u determines f ∈ π̂_{0,3} only modulo left multiplication by powers l_0^n (n ∈ Ẑ), because u is an outer automorphism.
2. Map f to SL(2,Ẑ)/±1, giving (r s; t u) mod sign.
3. Formula (79): l_0^n acts by left multiplication by (1 −2n; 0 1). This changes only the top row, to (r − 2nt, s − 2nu), and leaves the bottom row (t,u) unchanged.
4. Hence (t,u), and therefore u̲, are determined mod sign by u alone.

The same argument applies to the auxiliary matrix α_0 = (a b; c d). It is determined mod sign up to left multiplication by an l_0^n, so its bottom row (c,d) is canonical mod sign. This feeds the Eisenstein-type element cρ + d, whose norm is c² + cd + d² (the D of the next page).

On the next page Grothendieck tests the conjectural relation (80): u̲ = μ α(cρ + d) = μ f^{-1} l_0^{-ν} α_0(cρ + d), with a doubtful sign factor ε_?. He verifies it entrywise using det = 1 and the identity −1 + ε_2 μ u² = −ε_2 μ t².

Purpose: to describe explicitly the action of GT-type automorphisms on the congruence completion SL(2,Ẑ). The answer is inner by an element of GL(2,Ẑ) of determinant μ, i.e. through the 'cyclotomic' multiplier. The conjugating matrix lies in the normalizer of the Gaussian torus attached to the elliptic point i. It is linked to the Eisenstein torus attached to ρ through the bottom rows of f and α_0.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. Formula (79) is correct: left multiplication by an upper unipotent matrix preserves the bottom row. With l_0 ↦ (1 −2; 0 1), l_0^n ↦ (1 −2n; 0 1) is consistent.

Gap: the statement is only modulo sign. Grothendieck himself flags on the next page that the sign factors (ε_2, δ = ε_3) in relation (80) are not settled ('il y a lieu peut-être de corriger par un facteur ε_? quelque part').

ideas.what: The action of S_3-equivariant automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} (GT̂-type elements) on the congruence completion SL(2,Ẑ) is inner, given by conjugation by a matrix in GL(2,Ẑ) of determinant μ.
ideas.modern_name: Action of GT̂ / Gal(Q̄/Q) on the congruence completion of SL(2,Z) through the cyclotomic character
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in the Ihara / Nakamura / Lochak–Schneps circle (1990s): Galois acts on congruence quotients via the cyclotomic character
ideas.where_published: Not in the Esquisse d'un programme in this explicit form; La Longue Marche discusses Ŝ_{0,3} and SL(2,Z)^ but, as far as I know, not this formula.

ideas.what: Canonical construction, mod sign, of the conjugating matrix u̲ = μ(u, ε_2 t; −t, ε_2 u) from the bottom row (t,u) of the image of f in SL(2,Ẑ). Its invariance under f ↦ l_0^n f follows from (79).
ideas.modern_name: Image of the f-component of a GT element in the congruence quotient, made independent of the l_0-ambiguity (inner-automorphism ambiguity)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; no explicit standard reference known to me

ideas.what: The conjugating matrix normalizes the order-4 element σ_∞, so it is a Gaussian element u + ti with ε_2 μ(u² + t²) = 1. Its relation with the Eisenstein element cρ + d, of norm c² + cd + d², built from α_0, ties the f-component to the CM tori at the elliptic points i and ρ.
ideas.modern_name: Normalizers of elliptic (CM) tori Z[i]*, Z[ζ_3]* in GL(2,Ẑ) and their role in the GT action on torsion of SL(2,Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related ideas: Lochak–Schneps and Nakamura on GT̂ and torsion / the S_3-symmetry; unsure of an explicit match

missed.claim: Grothendieck obtains an explicit norm constraint: for an automorphism with multiplier μ, the bottom row (t,u) of the congruence image of f satisfies ε_2 μ(t² + u²) = 1 in Ẑ, a Gaussian-norm condition. He then relates it, through cρ + d, to an Eisenstein-norm quantity c² + cd + d². This links the GT action on SL(2,Ẑ) to the CM tori at i and ρ. The literature usually only says the action on congruence quotients is 'through the cyclotomic character', without such explicit matrix formulas tied to f.
missed.quote: on a beaucoup mieux encore, modulo signe, puisqu'on a pu définir canoniquement, en termes de u, la matrice u̲ par la formule (75)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives explicit constraints on the congruence image of f for GT̂ or Galois elements. These could be compared with known results on the image of f in Γ(2)^ / SL(2,Ẑ), for example in work on GT and modular / congruence towers.

missed.claim: The exact sign normalization in relation (80), u̲ = μ f^{-1} l_0^{-ν} α_0(cρ + d), is left unresolved when ε_2 = −1. The factors ε_2 and δ = ε_3 are flagged as needing correction.
missed.quote: tout au moins si ε_2 = 1 — sinon il y a lieu peut-être de corriger par un facteur ε_? quelque part
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor open bookkeeping point, but needed to make the formula a clean statement.

deep.surprise_reason: The overall fact (the GT/Galois action on the congruence completion is inner up to the cyclotomic multiplier) is essentially known. The explicit canonical construction of the conjugating matrix from the f-component, with its Gaussian/Eisenstein norm identities, is an unpublished detail that may not appear explicitly in the literature. This page itself only contains the routine invariance check (79).
transcription_corrections: Top of page: the '369' is Grothendieck's own page number written above the line; the line reads '(ce qui décrit l'action extérieure de u sur Sl(2,Ẑ)′ en termes des multiplicateurs μ)'.
'modulo signe' is an insertion above 'canoniquement', to be read 'puisqu'on a pu définir canoniquement, modulo signe, en termes de u, ...'.
'f ∈ π̂_{0,3}' (hat on π, lower-case pi) is consistent with the image; likewise 'l'auto. u de π̂_{0,3}'.
The left diagonal marginal note is barely legible; it seems to begin 'NB Pour vérifier ...' and 'On a fait ceci pour ...'. The transcription's [?] markers are appropriate.
The last line is 'cρ + d', written as the start of the continuation onto the next page.
